source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Engine Electrical, p.6Y-12

procedures.title: Voltage regulator: adjust voltage setting
steps: Adjust to 14.2 to 14.6 volts (adjusting screw, see figure 7c in the manual).
Unplug the four-terminal connector, refit the regulator cover, then plug the connector back in.
Keep running at 1500 rpm for 5-10 minutes so the regulator regains operating temperature.
Cycle the regulator by unplugging and replugging the connector and read voltage; 13.5 to 15.2 volts means a good regulator.
notes: Always unplug the four-terminal connector before removing or installing the regulator cover, to avoid short-circuit damage.

procedures.title: Delcotron output test (ammeter method)
steps: Disconnect the battery ground cable at the battery.
Disconnect the red wire at the Delcotron battery terminal and connect an ammeter in series between wire and terminal.
Connect a voltmeter from the battery terminal to a good ground on the generator.
Unplug the F-R connector at the Delcotron.
Jumper the Delcotron "F" terminal to its battery terminal.
Connect an adjustable carbon pile across the battery posts.
Start the engine, slowly raise speed to 1500 rpm while adjusting the carbon pile to hold 14 volts.
Read the amperage and compare with the specifications.
Turn off the ignition, disconnect the battery ground cable and remove all test equipment.
If output meets specification, the generator is not the problem; if not, remove it, bench test and repair.
notes: See figure 9c in the manual for connections.

procedures.title: Delcotron diode and field test
steps: Disconnect the battery ground cable at the battery.
Positive diodes (test A): read an ohmmeter between the "R" and "BAT" terminals, then reverse the leads and read again.
notes: These tests find a good, shorted or open field and a shorted diode, but not an open diode. If output was low and these tests pass, see Service Operations.
